explain.say: Why can a footballer earn more than a nurse, when nurses save lives? It feels unfair, so let's look closely. A wage is the money paid for work. Look at the board: four reasons that shape how much a job pays.

faq.q: Why are doctors paid so much?
faq.a: Doctors train for many years, carry big responsibility and are always needed, while the number of qualified doctors is limited. All of that pushes pay up.
asks: Why do doctors earn a lot?

faq.q: What is supply and demand for workers?
faq.a: Workers are like a market: if many people can do a job, employers can pay less; if few can and many employers want them, pay rises.
asks: How does the labour market work?

faq.a: A minimum wage is the lowest pay per hour or day that employers are allowed to pay by law. Supporters say it protects workers; critics worry a high one could reduce jobs. Evidence is debated.
A trade union is a group of workers who join together to bargain with employers for better pay, hours and safety. Unions are strong in countries like Sweden and Denmark.

faq.q: Why are men and women sometimes paid differently?
faq.a: Reasons include women more often working in lower-paid jobs or part-time, career breaks for caring, and sometimes unfair treatment. Many countries have laws requiring equal pay for equal work.
asks: What is the gender pay gap?

facts: The International Labour Organization, founded in 1919, sets international standards for work.
Germany introduced its first national minimum wage in 2015.
